definition: In this context, ethnic refers to belonging to a cultural group, such as an ethnic minority, that is linked by shared language, traditional writing, collective memory, identity, and values. These shared cultural features can shape psychological experience and distress when they are threatened or eroded.

reasons: The packet supports that the study concerns “ethnic minorities” and relates eroded languages/traditional scripts to continuity of collective memory, identity, and values, but it does not provide an explicit definition of “ethnic” as “belonging to a cultural group.”

The remaining elements of the definition (shared language/traditional scripts, continuity of collective memory/identity/values, and psychological distress when these are threatened/eroded) are broadly consistent with the packet text, but the overall definition includes the unsupported broader definitional framing noted above.
The packet supports ethnic minorities with endangered languages/scripts and associated cultural continuity, but it does not define “ethnic” generally as “belonging to a cultural group.”
“Traditional writing” is not stated in the packet; the source mentions traditional scripts.
The definition stretches a specific study context into a broad definitional claim, which is unsupported by the packet alone.
